Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the items we agreed we'd follow up on:

2) Vendor security questionnaire: you said you'd start the questionnaire. Please find attached our standard vendor questionnaire (we can also complete yours if you prefer).

   - Deletion SLA for customer-initiated full-data deletes (including backups/snapshots)
   - Backup retention and snapshot lifecycle (including cross-region copies)
   - Log retention policy (access logs, audit logs, request logs)

4) Encryption & backups: confirm encryption at rest/in transit and KMS usage for backups if applicable.

Next steps we proposed on the call: Redwood will share a short data_retention_matrix.xlsx and our SOC2 external letter; Amaya will kick off the vendor questionnaire and provide initial retention numbers so we can align on SLAs.

Can you confirm the items above and attach any current retention policy excerpts you can share? If it helps, we can schedule a 30-min security follow-up next week to iron out the deletion workflow.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly so procurement can proceed.

Hi Neha —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few quick notes from our side: 

- SOC 2: We are in the final remediation window for SOC 2 Type II with an expected completion date of 2026-09-15. We can provide our SOC 2 Type II in-progress attestation letter and an interim security overview (I will attach what I have).

- Vendor questionnaire: I'm attaching the questionnaire we mentioned (vendor_security_questionnaire.pdf). Our security team will start populating the sections; please complete the parts on your network/topology and backup encryption.

- Retention & deletion (initial numbers):
   • Backups/snapshots: retained for 90 days by default; snapshots are kept for 30 days before recycling. We maintain encrypted copies and replicate to a secondary region for DR.
   • Logs: access and audit logs retained for 180 days; request logs (application telemetry) retained for 90 days.
   • Deletion SLA: for customer-initiated full-data deletes we aim to remove primary data within 7 days (soft delete), but removal from backups/snapshots can take up to 30 days due to snapshot lifecycle. Full purge from replicated backups may be completed within 30-45 days depending on backup rotation.

- Encryption: Data is encrypted at rest using AES-256; backups use managed KMS keys. In-transit TLS 1.2+.

I'll attach what I can share; can you confirm whether those retention windows meet Redwood's standard deletion SLA (we saw references to 30 days in the docs) and whether you need a tighter SLA for backups?

Thanks — Javier

Thanks Javier — that's super helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions (so engineering/legal can scope):

1) When you say backups are "retained 90 days by default" and "snapshots 30 days", are snapshots included in the 90 days or are they a separate lifecycle? In other words, could a deleted object still exist in a snapshot beyond 90 days?

2) For the deletion SLA: is the 7-day soft-delete window a user-facing delay or an internal retention period before we trigger purge? We typically tell customers a max of 30 days for full purge including backups; if your snapshot rotation can guarantee 30 days max purge we can align on a 30-day SLA. Anything beyond 45 days will likely need legal sign-off.

3) KMS: can you confirm key ownership model (customer-managed KMS vs Amaya-managed) for backups? If customer-managed, please note any operational steps required for key rotation that would impact restores.

If it's useful, we can schedule a 30-min meeting with Rishi (security/engineering) next week to walk through the questionnaire and retention matrix. Rishi — are you available Wed/Thu afternoon PST?

Hi Marissa / Neha —

Answers below to your clarifying questions: 

1) Snapshots vs backups: Snapshots are point-in-time copies created from the primary dataset and have their own 30-day lifecycle. Backups (incremental/referenced for DR) are retained for 90 days. A deleted object could exist in a snapshot for up to 30 days beyond primary deletion, and in backups up to 90 days depending on which backup bucket the object was captured in. We do not keep immutable snapshots beyond those windows.

2) Deletion SLA: The 7-day soft-delete is an internal flag; customers can request immediate soft-delete but full purge from backup rotation will follow the snapshot/backup lifecycle (30-45 days for full purge). If you need contractually guaranteed purge within 30 days, we can discuss a targeted SLA (may incur additional charges).

3) KMS: Backups use Amaya-managed KMS by default. We offer customer-managed keys (CMK) for enterprise customers on request; with CMK, note that key revocation/rotation procedures must be coordinated to avoid restore failures.

4) Encryption & compliance: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit. We are also mapping GDPR and HIPAA applicability — Amaya is HIPAA-aware and supports BAAs for PHI workloads; for GDPR, DSRs are supported and we provide processes to locate and remove personal data on request (subject to the retention windows above).

5) Logs: Access/audit logs retained 180 days. Application request telemetry retained 90 days. We can provide sampled log exports for longer-term analytics if required (will need a separate arrangement).

Next steps: 
- We will start populating your vendor_security_questionnaire.pdf and upload an initial version by EOD Wed 2026-05-14.
- We'll share the SOC 2 interim attestation/letter via secure Drive link (expect to have the attestation doc by 2026-05-20).
- If Redwood needs a 30-day contractual purge guarantee, pls flag that now so we can route to our legal/ops for a potential amendment.

Regards,
Amaya Security Team
